design: Traction motor types and disassembled Jaguar I-Pace PMSM
why: Provides a visual overview of motor architecture and component access.

design: Motor components and disassembly sequence
why: Useful for explaining general disassemblability, but it is a 3-kW brake motor rather than an EV traction motor.

design: SPMSM, SynRM and PM-assisted SynRM topologies
why: Useful for distinguishing motor and rotor topology visually.

design: Ford Fusion HF35 transmission and motor access
why: Shows why magnet recovery begins with access through a larger transmission assembly.

design: Toyota and Mazda motors, rotors and IPM arrangements
why: Directly shows two EV motor architectures and buried magnet configurations.

design: Connectors and precision-fit features
why: Shows concrete design features that obstruct disassembly.

design: Rotor-stator contact and offset conditions
why: Useful schematic for explaining why rotor-stator separability is a distinct evaluation stage.

design: PMSM rotor anatomy with buried magnets, shaft, bearings, balancing disc and stack segments
why: One of the clearest visuals for rotor-level design variables in the knowledge base.

design: Buried magnet and lamination-stack geometry
why: Useful for explaining geometric variability and magnet-pocket access.

design: Surface-mounted and buried PM rotor topologies
why: Direct visual comparison of the main magnet-accessibility distinction.

design: Adhesive-based rotor/magnet assembly
why: Shows how a manufacturing joint becomes an end-of-life separation barrier.

design: Surface and buried magnet laboratory component configurations
why: Clearly shows bonded area, embedment and the geometry used to generate evidence.

design: Exploded/interior view, end cap and assembled proposed IPM rotor
why: Very clear visual of modular rotor construction, magnet location, bolts and end-cap retention.

design: Cross-section comparing conventional IPM rotor and proposed rib-less modular rotor
why: Direct visual comparison of iron ribs, magnet enclosure and the rib-less design concept.

design: Prototype rotor components before assembly and assembled machine
why: Shows that the modular rotor exists physically and exposes the separable rotor modules and caps.

design: Progression from one shaped magnet to standardised reusable magnet segments
why: Useful visual for geometry standardisation and cross-generation reuse compatibility.

design: Four motor/rotor concepts for different magnet reuse strategies
why: Useful for showing how magnet integration changes across rotor architectures.

design: Real EV component rotors with steel cover plates and visible magnets after cover removal
why: One of the strongest real-product images showing a physical design barrier to magnet access.

design: Comparison of caulking, press-fit, spring, adhesive and injection-moulded magnet fixation approaches
why: Excellent design reference for the fixation-method variable without focusing on recovery equipment.

design: IPM rotor cross-section and flux-barrier cavity proposed for reversible interlayer fixation
why: Shows where a fixation/release feature could be integrated into an IPM rotor.

design: Solid bread-loaf magnet pole versus segmented standard-sized magnet concept
why: Useful visual for explaining magnet geometry standardisation and reuse compatibility.

design: Claw-pole rotor and the magnet slit that terminates at the inter-claw
why: Directly shows the geometry that obstructs the magnet's exit path.

design: Commercial hub motor, motor without end-shields, stator and rotor
why: Useful real-motor assembly view for general disassemblability and component hierarchy.

design: Four DEMETER motor concepts: outer-rotor, 3D-flux hybrid, claw-pole and radial IPM
why: Useful design comparison showing how motor architecture and magnet integration vary across concepts.

design: Exploded permanent-magnet synchronous motor showing rotor, stator, housing, bearings, resolver and end plates
why: A clear automotive-relevant motor assembly view for explaining general component hierarchy and separability.

design: Selective Tesla Model Y EDU disassembly map down to the rotor core
why: Shows the actual dependency chain between phase terminals, resolver, motor module and rotor access.

design: Disassembled Tesla Model Y EDU with inverter, transmission, heat exchanger, stator and rotor core
why: Strong real-product image showing the major separable subsystems and their relative integration.

design: Typical fully integrated electric axle drive with motor, gearbox, inverter, bearing shields and rotor/stator components
why: Useful design reference for integration degree and main subsystem boundaries in an automotive traction unit.

design: Schematic dismantling hierarchy from integrated drive unit to motor, rotor, stator, shaft, windings and magnets
why: Useful visual for distinguishing general disassembly levels from the later magnet-recovery stage.

design: Exploded electric traction-drive unit with rotor, stator, transmission, power electronics, housing and end plate
why: Clear architecture image for general disassemblability and subsystem integration.

design: Magnet mounting techniques and different internal magnet arrangements
why: Useful design reference for separating magnet topology from fixation method.

design: Photographic sequence from outer traction-drive housing through gearbox removal to rotor extraction
why: Strong real-assembly visual showing hidden fasteners, preceding components and rotor-access dependency.

design: Disassembly demonstrator with a close-up of the Volkswagen rotor and unscrewing tool
why: The rotor close-up is useful for showing the real axial screw-retention architecture, although the overall figure is partly automation-focused.

design: Manually disassembled Volkswagen ID.3 and e.go traction motors
why: Strong real-product visual showing two automotive traction-motor assemblies that were physically analysed for joining methods.

design: Simplified motor parts plus graph representation and a real 25-part motor model
why: Useful for explaining how a motor design can be represented as parts and connections for model-based disassembly evaluation.
